opportunities.title: Regional General Manager Airports
opportunities.description:
Why WestJet

Since our story took off in 1996, WestJet has strived to enrich the lives of everyone in our world; a career with us is no exception. Weâre proud to be one of Canadaâs most admired and respected corporate cultures and continuously aim for the highest standards of service and success.

Join us, this is where your career story takes off.

This position is eligible for remote work, within Canada, under our mobile workforce program.

Regional General Manager, Airports

As the Regional General Manager, you will provide strategic leadership and direction to deliver safe operations while driving excellence in operational performance and guest service through our contracted service partners across the designated region. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Airports, you will lead a team of Regional Managers and collaborate closely with internal and external stakeholders to maintain regulatory compliance, foster positive relationships, and ensure a consistent, high-quality guest experience across all airport touchpoints within the region.

This role requires an experienced leader who holds service partners accountable for delivering WestJet's operational and service standards while balancing the needs of our guests, our partners, and our business. You will coach and support service partners in developing and executing airport action plans that address performance gaps, strengthen safety, and improve the guest experience.

The Regional General Manager will provide strategic oversight of airport operations across the region by identifying emerging risks, monitoring operational performance, and ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's standards and priorities. Through strong partnerships with service providers and airport authorities, you will drive continuous improvement, enhance operational resilience, and ensure our airports consistently deliver safe, reliable operations and an exceptional guest experience.

Key Deliverables Include

  • Foster a Safety Above All culture with Regional Managers by ensuring service partners achieve safety targets, monitoring performance trends, and addressing operational risks.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Regional Managers to deliver operational performance, guest satisfaction, employee engagement, and financial results.
  • Provide strategic oversight of airport operations, ensuring consistent execution of WestJet's operational and guest standards and priorities.
  • Deliver regional operational performance by achieving operational, guest experience, and financial objectives while driving continuous improvement through station action plans.
  • Provide governance through audits, operational reviews, and performance assessments to ensure adherence to standards, identify risks, and drive corrective actions.
  • Analyze operational performance and safety data to identify trends and risks, inform operational decision making, prioritize resources, and strengthen oversight across the region.
  • Serve as the senior escalation point for Regional Managers, providing leadership and decision support for complex operational, guest, commercial, safety, and irregular operations.
  • Partner with the Strategic Procurement team to develop service partner strategies, support partner selection, and ensure service partners deliver safe, high-performing, and cost-effective operations.
  • Build and maintain executive relationships with airport authorities, service partner leadership, government agencies, bargaining agents, and other key stakeholders.
  • Lead regional operational planning to ensure airports are resourced and operationally ready for seasonal demand, network growth, start-ups, restarts, service partner transitions, station closures, and other strategic initiatives.
  • Champion innovation and continuous improvement by leveraging data and implementing initiatives that enhance operational performance, the guest experience, employee engagement, and financial results.
  • Participate as a member of the Airports Leadership Team to establish departmental priorities, contribute to strategic direction, and lead the development and execution of departmental initiatives.

Experience And Qualifications

  • 3+ years Airports leadership experience required
  • Business leadership experience with a significant level of internal and external dependencies and relationships.
  • Possess strong business acumen to deliver departmental plans including budget.
  • Proven ability to multitask & handle changing priorities.
  • Confident in presenting materials and reports to the next 2 levels.
  • Post-secondary education with a business application an asset.
  • Ability to manage multiple leaders and locations simultaneously.
  • Proficient in PC based applications, Microsoft Project, Word, Excel and Outlook.
  • Ability to travel & spend time away for significant periods of time.
  • Project management skills considered an asset.
  • Knowledge of International regulations and guidelines (for example - TSA/Civil Aviation, UK High Commission etc.) an asset.
  • Proven track record of effectively influencing leadership teams via handling partners and developing strong direct leadership teams.
  • IATA SGHA experience would be beneficial.

The Benefits Of Being a WestJetter

WestJet provides all WestJetters with a competitive total rewards package. On top of that, we offer:

  • A fun and friendly culture with colleagues who work together to win
  • Travel privileges for you and your family, effective from your start date
  • Savings and Benefit programs that are flexible to meet your specific needs

Think weâre a great fit? Apply now!

About WestJet Group Of Companies

WestJet took to the skies in 1996 with just over 200 employees and three aircraft operating service to five destinations. Since then, WestJet has pioneered low-cost travel in Canada, cutting airfares in half, and increasing the flying population in Canada by more than 50 per cent. Since the Sunwing Airlines integration in 2025, more than 15,000 WestJetters support nearly 200 aircraft and connect guests to our global network of more than 100 destinations across North America, Central America, the Caribbean, Europe and Asia. The WestJet Group is a major Canadian employer and includes WestJet Airlines, WestJet Encore and Sunwing Vacations Group. Weâre Canadaâs leading value airline and largest vacation provider, with a united purpose of providing affordable and accessible air and vacation travel to Canadians.

Our safety promise

At WestJet, the safety and security of our people and our guests is a core value and at the heart of what we do. Safety and security are shared responsibilities all team members are expected to use safe work practices to ensure their well-being and the safety of others. WestJet recognizes that the use of Alcohol and Drugs can adversely impact a safe work environment and the well-being of others including guests, suppliers and the public, as well as place WestJet's operations at risk. All roles that are identified as Safey-Sensitive are required to pass a Pre-Employment Alcohol and Drug Test as per WestJet'sâ¯Alcohol and Drug Policy.â¯

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We embrace what makes each of us unique, and what makes us uniquely WestJet. We welcome diverse skills, experiences and backgrounds so if you're passionate about this role, we encourage you to apply â even if you don't meet every qualification listed. WestJet is committed to inclusiveness, equity and accessibility throughout the selection process. If you require accommodation at any stage, please contact our Talent Acquisition team at talent@westjet.com.

We value the time and effort you put into your application. Our recruitment process is highly competitive and while every applicant will receive communication regarding their application status, only those selected to move forward will be contacted with next steps. If this role isnât the right fit, we encourage you to explore future opportunities with us.

About

For more information about everything WestJet, please visit westjet.com/aboutus.

If you wish to withdraw your application or request that your personal information be deleted, please contact us at talent@westjet.com.

opportunities.title: Sales Development Representative Outbound
opportunities.description:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.

Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2.

Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. Weâre a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agreesâ our employee NPS is in the high 80s.

About The Role

As a Sales Development Representative, your primary responsibility will be to secure meetings with top prospective companies and individuals. You'll work closely with one paired Account Executive to generate meetings from their target account list. We encourage account development through outbound prospecting, social selling, networking, attending conferences and field marketing events, and any sales activity that would contribute to expanding the Tremendous brand. You will be the first line of engagement with prospective customers and will have an impact on Tremendousâ revenue growth and future success.

What You'll Do

  • Work primarily to bring in new deals through Outbound prospecting.
  • Collaborate with Account Executives, as well as members of our Marketing and Customer Success teams, to develop new strategies to build our sales pipeline and grow our business.
  • Use Outreach, LinkedIn, your own network, and other prospecting tools to research accounts, identify key contacts and craft targeted messaging.
  • Learn our technology and effectively communicate our value proposition. Work to understand their goals and challenges to better understand how we can help.

What You'll Bring

  • 2-3 years of prior sales experience, ideally in a similar outbound or SDR role.
  • Clever and creative problem solving. We're small and emphasize output and iteration over a sales handbook set in stone.
  • Independence. We all work together to solve tough problems here at Tremendous, but taking pride in experimenting and finding your own answers is the best way to learn.
  • Collaboration. When our SDRs uncover new trends and tactics that work to set meetings, they share them with their teammates so everyone can benefit.
  • Ability to thrive with a well-set quota. We want our goals to be fair and achievable. You should find these goals alongside your team and with your manager and use them as a benchmark for success.
  • Ambition. Ambition isn't a dirty word at Tremendous. We're a team of achievers collaborating on a fast-growing product and that means personal growth in both role and responsibility as well as tons of personal upside for you.

What's Cool About The Role

  • You'll work at a company growing quickly yet sustainably. Weâre profitable with plenty more opportunity ahead. Thatâs good news for your career growth.
  • Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role: $65,000 - $70,000 plus commission.
  • Real benefits. 100% covered health (US), unlimited PTO, 12-16 weeks paid parental leave.
  • Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas.
  • Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook.

Location

This role is remote-first and you can work wherever you want in the Americas. That said, we have a preference for SDRs based in the Austin or New York areas. There may be opportunities to train and collaborate together in person throughout the year.

Compensation Range: $65K - $70K

opportunities.description:
Who we are:

MasterClass is the platform where the worldâs best come together so anyone, anywhere, can access and be inspired by their knowledge and stories. We put you in the room with the creators, thinkers, makers and leaders who have changed the world, so that you can change yours.

MasterClass Executive is our selective, cohort-based program for senior professionals learning to lead in the AI era, taught by world-class operators and academics in collaboration with the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and OpenAI. Admission is competitive: applications are reviewed individually, and spots in each cohort are limited.

Â 

About the Role:

We're hiring an Admissions Advisor as a temporary, full-time employee to support our next enrollment cycle. You'll spend most of your day on the phone and in the inbox with applicants and admitted candidates â answering questions about the program experience, helping them weigh the value of enrolling, and guiding them from admission to enrollment ahead of cohort deadlines. You'll also support employer-sponsored enrollment: equipping candidates to make the case to their company and responding to inquiries from managers, HR, and L&D teams.

This is a high-volume, goal-driven role during our busiest enrollment windows. The ideal candidate is a natural on the phone â consultative, warm, and credible with senior professionals â and genuinely fluent in both AI and the business-education landscape. You know what programs like ours cost, what the alternatives promise, and how to have an honest conversation about fit and value.

Â 

Â What You Will Do:

  • Own a high volume of admissions calls â scheduled consultations and proactive outreach with applicants and admitted candidates â answering questions about the curriculum, live sessions, AI Labs, in-person intensive, time commitment, and cohort experience
  • Help prospective enrollees evaluate the program's value: speak confidently and accurately to outcomes, program fees, and payment options, and position MasterClass Executive honestly against the alternatives candidates are weighing (executive education, MBA programs, certificates, and cohort-based courses)
  • Guide admitted candidates from decision to enrollment with timely phone and email follow-up through each enrollment window, identifying and removing blockers before deadlines
  • Run point on employer-sponsorship communications: respond to sponsorship inquiries, provide candidates with materials to secure company support (manager emails, ROI summaries, program overviews), and flag multi-enrollee company interest to our partnerships team

  • Genuinely energized by phone time: you listen first, handle objections without a hard sell, and are comfortable with 20â30+ meaningful conversations a day
  • A strong writer who can run a high-volume inbox with responses that are crisp, warm, and never read like a template

  • Organized and self-directed: strong CRM hygiene, pipeline discipline, and comfort being measured against clear goals

opportunities.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW:


Society 18 is seeking a highly organized, creative, and proactive Associate of Events, Social & Influencer Marketing to support the agency's creator partnerships, experiential marketing initiatives, social media presence, and day-to-day operations.


This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, loves bringing ideas to life, enjoys wearing multiple hats, and is passionate about influencer marketing, social media, events, and creator culture. The Associate will work cross-functionally across events, social media, talent, partnerships, and operations while helping execute high-impact campaigns and experiences for creators and brand partners.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


Social Media Marketing & Content Creation

  • Manage day-to-day content planning for Society 18's Instagram and LinkedIn channels.
  • Develop monthly content calendars aligned with agency campaigns, partnerships, creator announcements, and events.
  • Write engaging social media copy, captions, and assist with music selection for short-form content.
  • Design graphics in Canva, including creator announcements, milestone graphics, birthday posts, event promotions, partnership assets, and press announcements.
  • Film and edit Instagram Reels, creator spotlights, event recap videos, and partnership content using CapCut.
  • Maintain Instagram feed planning and overall visual consistency.
  • Schedule and publish content across social media platforms.
  • Publish Instagram Stories daily.
  • Engage with creators, brand partners, and community members through comments and direct messages.
  • Maintain creator posting trackers to ensure balanced representation across agency channels.
  • Develop quarterly newsletters and email marketing campaigns in Flodesk.
  • Create LinkedIn content highlighting agency partnerships, company milestones, leadership updates, and industry news.
  • Build and maintain creator pages on the Society 18 website.
  • Update creator biographies, follower counts, categories, and roster information as needed.


Event Production & Experiential Marketing

  • Capture behind-the-scenes photo and video content for real-time social media coverage.
  • Create post-event recap presentations in Canva and track creator coverage using Archive.


Influencer Marketing & Brand Partnerships

  • Pitch creators for brand activations, networking events, creator trips, fashion weeks, festivals, and industry experiences, including ESSENCE Festival, New York Fashion Week, Coachella, and other cultural moments.
  • Support creator onboarding by updating internal databases, website profiles, onboarding materials, and social media assets.
  • Assist with proactive creator pitching for paid brand partnerships.
  • Support talent scouting initiatives and maintain the agency's talent scouting database.
  • Research new creators, emerging trends, and partnership opportunities.


Executive & Administrative Operations

  • Coordinate meetings, calendars, and scheduling with creators, brands, vendors, and internal team members.
  • Prepare meeting agendas, capture notes, and distribute follow-up action items.
  • Maintain internal databases, presentations, production trackers, reporting dashboards, and operational documents.
  • Research and source brand contacts across beauty, fashion, travel, hospitality, wellness, food & beverage, and lifestyle industries using Apollo, Airtable, LinkedIn, and additional research tools.
  • Support day-to-day agency operations and assist with special projects as assigned.


QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Event Management, Business, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 1â3 years of experience in influencer marketing, social media, events, talent management, PR, or a related field.
  • Exceptional organizational skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong creative eye for branding, design, and social content.
  • Comfortable working both independently and collaboratively.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:


The ideal candidate is creative, resourceful, highly organized, and excited to help build meaningful experiences for creators and brand partners. They enjoy bringing ideas to life, solving problems, collaborating across teams, and staying on top of emerging social and cultural trends. They are equally comfortable planning an event, editing a Reel, coordinating logistics, mentoring interns, or supporting creator partnershipsâalways with a positive attitude and strong attention to detail.

opportunities.title: This IS Your Dream Job
opportunities.description:
Here are two questions to ask yourself: 1) when are you most content? (Not âhappyâ per se, since happy moments are fleeting. 2) Does contentment ever happen for you during the workday?

The average American worker spends 2080 hours per year on paid work. Over 30 years, that adds up to 62,400 hours. Thatâs a LOT of time to spend doing something you donât like doing.

Research also shows that people will change careers at least 7 times during their lifetime. However, career changes arenât always drastic â you can change the focus of your daily work activity without changing jobs. Sometimes incremental shiftsâsmall changes in what you do and how you do itâare the best and most satisfying way to land that dream job

The key is to concentrate on ways to shift paid job duties into activities that give you that feeling of contentment.

Grab a Sheet Of Paper And a Pencilâor Open Up Your Favorite Word Processor And Work Through The Following Steps To Come Up With Your Own Action Plan To Realize Your Dream Job

STEP 1: Think about your current job â make a list of the tasks that comprise your job. Highlight the ones you most enjoy performing in your job. Note the ones you canât stand

STEP 2: Make a list of activities youâve done in the past that you are most proud of, and that you got the most satisfaction from. These can come from previous jobs, volunteer activities, school work, or hobbies. If you loved laying out the college newspaper, but hated the organizational aspects such as chasing people down to get their content in on time, then that tells you something about the types of activities that work for you.

STEP 3: Envision your ideal job â and list the tasks that it would encompass. What basic skills involved in your ideal job could start working on today? This could be something simple â if your ideal job is to be in charge of all written communication for your organization, an area you could start working on immediately is your writing skills. Even if your current writing skills are pretty good, there is always room to work towards a higher level of achievement.

STEP 4: Now take the list of tasks and activities from steps 1 & 2 above, along with the list of skills from step 3, and group them into functions related to your job that you could concentrate on. (For example, if you are a financial analyst, but you find the grind of financial reports tedious, but you love creating charts and graphs and putting together presentations that visually demonstrate trends â your tasks and activities list could include âcreating graphs & chartsâ, and one skill that could be on your list is âEnhance MS Excel charting & graphing skillsâ.

STEP 5: Conduct some research into the training available out there that would help you to enhance the skills you outlined in step 3. This could involve a number of options â anything from volunteering with an organization in a capacity where you could practice your skills, to taking webinars, intensive workshops, certificate programs, or working toward a degree.

STEP 6: Using the information you gathered in step 5 above, get started with the training program(s) that will meet your individual needs. Remember that you can start small and fine-tune your training plan as you go along. You can also mix and match various training components â it doesnât have to be a straight path, as long as it gets you to where you want to go. Get involved with online forums and interest groups that will help you learn more about the latest techniques in your area of interest. As you spend more time learning and practicing, your skills will improve.

Never underestimate the value of volunteering without asking for additional compensationâ¦your boss and superiors will be impressed that you are interested enough to take on a project without asking for something in return. Showcase your best efforts by volunteering to work on projects that will give you a chance to demonstrate your expertise.

Land Mines to Avoid

Being your own worst enemy â downplaying your talents wonât get you noticed or into consideration for that great new project. Toot your own horn and let others know that you are good at xyz (in the example above, creating charts and graphs). Just as important, offer to help others with that task â soon you will become the resident expert, the one that others turn to for help and advice on this topic

Being finished with learning â remember learning doesnât stop because you have that framed diploma. Keep taking courses, attending seminars and staying in touch with others in your field so that you stay at the leading edge of knowledge and practice in your area of interest

Getting stuck in a rut â Sometimes it seems easier to lay low and just plod along. But you canât stay still â keep looking for new opportunities to apply your talents and showcase them in new and interesting ways.

Decide what you like (and what you donât), do your homework, work hard at new opportunities and advertise the resultsâbefore you know it, youâll be living your dream job.

Contributor: Julie Clarke, Vancouver Island University (www.pr.viu.ca/techcomm)

opportunities.title: Ship to Shore Technician
opportunities.description:
Job Description

As a Ship-to-Shore Technician, you will play a vital role in supporting the safe and efficient operation of vessels arriving and departing at the port. This position involves working on the dock to ensure the proper mooring, securing, and release of ships, while maintaining safety and operational standards. In addition to mooring responsibilities, the role will also involve performing general maintenance and support tasks as required to ensure overall port and equipment readiness.

The Ship-to-Shore Technician is responsible for, but not limited to the following:

Docking and Undocking Operations

  • Assist in safely docking and undocking cruise ships at port using mooring lines, ropes, and related equipment.
  • Work in coordination with the shipâs captain, crew, and port authorities to ensure that vessels are safely secured and aligned with docking infrastructure.

Mooring Line Management:

  • Handle and manage mooring lines, ensuring they are properly fastened, tense, and released.
  • Perform visual inspection of mooring lines and related equipment regularly for wear and damage, ensuring everything is in safe working condition. (Regularly performed by ship crew)

Ship and Dock Safety

  • Maintain safety protocols during mooring procedures, ensuring that all tasks are performed in accordance with safety regulations.
  • Monitor weather conditions and report any changes that could affect docking or undocking procedures.

Communication and Coordination

  • Communicate effectively with other team members on board and shore-based personnel.
  • Work with the Port Authorities to ensure the timely and safe transfer of passengers and cargo.

Emergency Procedures

  • Be trained to respond in case of an emergency during docking or undocking operations, including accidents or hazardous situations.
  • Ensure all mooring operations are conducted efficiently and safely, even under adverse weather conditions or emergencies.

PPE Equipment (MANDATORY)

  • Must always be in possession of steel toe boots (or prescribed non-slip safety shoes), safety vest, hard hat, gloves, radio/communication device. (To be provided by Carnival)

Cleaning & Maintenance of Pier & Mooring Equipment & Fixtures:

  • Ensure all mooring equipment such as winches, ropes, and fenders are properly maintained and operational (through visual checks and inspections).
  • Gangway Inspections & Maintenance: Inspect gangway components for wear, corrosion, proper tension, secure connections, and smooth operation to ensure safe pedestrian access and functionality.
  • Fenders: Conduct visual inspections of pier fenders and associated hardware to identify cracks, deformation, excessive wear, or damage caused by vessel contact, and report deficiencies as needed.
  • Mooring Bollards: Regularly inspect mooring bollards for structural integrity, including corrosion, cracks, loose anchor bolts, foundation stress, and coating condition, to ensure safe vessel mooring.
  • Stanchions & Pier Fixtures: Inspect stanchions and associated components for corrosion, damage, misalignment, or instability, ensuring they remain secure and serviceable.
  • Ropes: Inspect ropes for wear, fraying, or damage, and verify they are properly positioned and suitable for continued use.
  • Mooring Equipment Maintenance: Perform minor maintenance and repairs of mooring equipment when necessary.
  • Pier & Dock Cleaning: Maintain clean, safe, and non-slip pier surfaces by removing dirt, salt, algae, stains, debris and other buildup by pressure washing and using prescribed cleaning equipment and solutions, along all designated cruise pier and trestle areas.
  • Cleaning Equipment Operation: Safely inspect, operate, and maintain cleaning equipment, including scrubbers and pressure washers, ensuring proper use, cleaning, and storage after each operation.

Additional Maintenance Support Activities

  • Perform minor maintenance support to technical teams including plumbing, electrical, masonry, carpentry, and HVAC functions.

Mandatory Training:

  • Maintain compliance with organizational requirements by attending and participating in all required company training sessions.

Lagoon Care

  • Perform maintenance/inspections of lagoon systems.

Education:

  • Education: High School Diploma.
  • Maintenance knowledge is preferred.
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) required within 6 months of employment start.
  • Three to Five years' experience working in a mooring or associated fields.

Essential Experience Required:

Must be physically fit. Must have strong customer service skills. Ability to work in an outdoor environment. Ability to multi-task and think critically. Previous work experience preferred. Prolonged periods standing and working outside. Must be able to lift, up to 50 pounds at times. All island employees must be physically able to participate in emergency lifesaving procedures and drills. Full use/range of motion of arms and legs as well as full visual, verbal and hearing abilities are required to receive and give instructions in the event of an emergency. Ability to read and write English to understand and interpret written procedures. This includes the ability to give and receive instructions in written and verbal forms and to effectively present information and respond to questions from guests, managers, and co-workers.

opportunities.title: Program & Events Coordinator
opportunities.description:
About the LSPA: The LSP Association (LSPA) is a non-profit association for Massachusetts Licensed Site Professionals (LSPs) and other related environmental practitioners who work on behalf of property owners, operators, and other involved parties to assess and cleanup oil and hazardous materials (OHM) released to the environment. LSPs are licensed by the Commonwealth to oversee this work and, since 1993, over 40,000 contaminated properties have been brought into regulatory compliance.


The LSPA's mission is to support our membership in achieving and maintaining a high standard of practice in the assessment and remediation of contaminated sites in Massachusetts and New England. The LSPA provides technical and educational resources to our membership in the form of programming, networking events, committees, and resources. The LSPA also serves as an advocate to the profession with MassDEP, the LSP Board of Registration, and the state legislature, and as a resource to the public.


Job Description: The Program & Events Coordinator plays a critical role in the success of the LSPA and serves as a primary point of contact for our members, volunteers, and sponsors. This individual is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing the association's educational programs and networking events, administering the sponsorship program, and providing customer service support. Success in this position means delivering high-quality member experiences, maintaining strong relationships with volunteers and sponsors, and ensuring the smooth administration of our continuing education program.


The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, customer-focused, and comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously. This individual enjoys working independently while collaborating closely with volunteers, board members, speakers, sponsors, and staff.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Educational Programs: Coordinate, plan, and manage programs and speakers for all LSPA courses, membership meetings, emerging professional events, the Annual Fall Party, and the Environmental Symposium. The LSPA hosts one to three events per month with 25-250 people in attendance. Approximately 65% of programming is hosted virtually. Content creation is performed in conjunction with input from the Executive Director, Committee Chairs, Education Committee, and Board of Directors.
  • Event Logistics: For in-person events, source event venues and help facilitate contracts; plan food and beverage, room set-up, and audiovisual needs; reconcile venue bills; and serve as the point of contact on-site. For virtual programs, setup and run the virtual meeting platform, monitor attendance and engagement, create moderator scripts and slides, and train speakers on how to use the virtual platform.
  • Continuing Education (CE) Administration: Compile CE materials for all educational courses and meetings; submit materials for credit approval with the LSP Board of Registration, the Connecticut Licensed Environmental Professional (LEP) Board, and other Boards/entities; maintain CE records related to attendance, engagement, and evaluation; issue certificates of attendance to attendees; and attend monthly virtual LSP Board of Registration meetings.
  • Sponsorship: Help administer the corporate and event sponsorship program, including updating the sponsorship prospectus, facilitating invoices/payments, maintaining contact lists, conducting outreach, and working with sponsors to access their sponsorship benefits.
  • Member Service and Organizational Support: Help monitor and respond to inquiries received through the organization email inbox; provide customer service to members, sponsors, speakers, and event attendees; attend Board meetings, leadership meetings, and committee meetings as requested; and support association operations and special projects as needed.


Qualifications

The person hired for this role should have the following qualifications:


Experience:

  • 2-5 years of experience in program/event planning, project management, or another related field.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and proven ability to provide excellent customer service.
  • Strong project management skills with excellent attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines independently.
  • Comfortable coordinating, building relationships with, and communicating professionally with members, volunteers, sponsors, vendors, and other external stakeholders/partners.


Technology:

  • Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Zoom Meetings and Zoom Webinar, including coordinating presenters from multiple locations, incorporating polling, and managing technical issues.
  • Association management systems (AMS) or member databases.
  • Online registration and evaluation platforms.
  • Canva or similar design tools (preferred, not required).

Preferred Qualifications (not required):

  • Experience working for a nonprofit organization, professional association, or membership-based organization.
  • Experience with the environmental sciences industry.
  • Familiarity with sponsorship development or relationship management.
  • Bachelor's degree, Associate's degree with relevant experience, or significant relevant professional experience demonstrating the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the position successfully.

Why Join the LSPA?

This is an opportunity to work with a respected association that supports environmental professionals making a meaningful impact on public health and environmental protection throughout Massachusetts and New England. As a small organization, we offer autonomy, flexibility, and the opportunity to build relationships with industry leaders while helping shape the educational and professional development experiences of our members. Compensation and benefits include:

  • Salary: The salary range for this position is $70,000â$80,000 annually. Compensation will be based on a variety of factors such as individual qualifications and experience.
  • Benefits: LSPA employees receive $300 per month for a Healthcare Reimbursement Account (HRA) that may be used to reimburse certain medical and insurance-related expenses. The organization does not currently offer group health or dental insurance plans. In addition, employees have access to a 401(k) plan.
  • PTO: 15 days of paid time off (PTO) annually for the first three years (increases to 20 days thereafter). The LSPA also provides 14 holidays per year (inclusive of 5 floating holidays).
  • Fully remote position: Candidates may reside anywhere in New England, with preference given to Massachusetts-based applicants. Travel to Massachusetts-based programs and events approximately 10â12 times annually is required.
  • Reimbursement for home office expenses: $750 annually.


How to Apply

Please submit a cover letter and resume to mmorris@lspa.org. Applications without cover letters or that request compensation/benefits beyond what we can provide will not be reviewed.


The LSPA is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, contact mmorris@lspa.org.


The LSPA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

Description

At ScionHealth, we empower our caregivers to do what they do best. We value every voice by caring deeply for every patient and each other. We show courage by running toward the challenge and we lean into new ideas by embracing curiosity and question asking. Together, we create our culture by living our values in our day-to-day interactions with our patients and teammates.

Job Summary

The Patient Access & Intake Coordinator plays a key role in facilitating a smooth and efficient patient admission process. This position provides vital administrative and operational support to the Business Development team and the Central Access and Authorizations Team (CAAT), ensuring timely initiation and management of referral activity.

Responsible for launching the referral management process, the coordinator oversees admission workflows, gathers and verifies required documentation, coordinates information for necessary approvals, and communicates essential information to relevant departments. Acting as a central liaison between Business Development, facility leadership, and CAAT colleagues, this coordinates admission logistics, confirm readiness to receive the patient, and ensure all clinical and operational details are aligned prior to arrival.

This role actively contributes to quality improvement, problem solving, and productivity initiatives within an interdisciplinary team model, demonstrating accountability and a commitment to operational excellence.

opportunities.title: Chief of Staff the CEO
opportunities.description:
The job in one line

You run the CEO's operating system: goals, cadence, and follow-through. You also personally own the projects that don't have a home yet.

Everyday Dose is moving fast in a lot of directions at once. The constraint isn't ideas or effort. It's making sure the right handful of things get set, tracked, and actually finished while everything else keeps running.

That's this job. It is not an executive assistant role and it is not a note-taking role. You'll own outcomes, run the meeting the leadership team is accountable to, and have a real seat.

What You'll Actually Do

Own goal setting. Run quarterly and annual planning end to end. Sit with each exec, turn intent into targets that are measurable and few. Hold the line when a goal is a paragraph instead of a number. Publish it so the whole company knows what we're playing for.

Manage against those goals. Goals decay the week after they're written unless someone owns them. You're that someone. You track progress, surface slippage early, and escalate the things that need the CEO before they become fires.

Run the weekly leadership meeting. Set the agenda, bring the numbers, drive to decisions. Every meeting ends with owners and dates, and you chase them down between meetings. You're not the scribe; you're the person who makes the hour worth everyone's time.

Keep the scoreboard honest. Build and maintain the company-level reporting leadership runs on, in partnership with finance and data. Numbers come from the warehouse, not from someone's recollection on a call. If two sources disagree, you're the one who reconciles them.

Run special projects. The high-stakes, cross-functional thing that has no owner: a new bet, a partnership, a channel or business we're deciding whether to enter, a problem that spans three teams and belongs to none of them. You get handed ambiguity and come back with an answer, a model, and a plan.

Be the CEO's second read. Pressure-test decisions before they're made. Prep board and investor materials. Write the memo when the thinking needs to be sharp. Say the thing nobody else in the room will say.

What Success Looks Like In 90 Days

  • Company goals for the quarter are written, owned, and measurable, and every leader can recite theirs without opening a doc
  • The weekly leadership meeting has a repeatable format, a live scoreboard, and decisions that stick
  • One company-level dashboard everyone trusts, sourced from the warehouse
  • Two special projects taken from ambiguous to finished without supervision
  • The CEO's time visibly reallocated toward the highest-leverage work in the business

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • 8 to 12 years of experience, including time as a Chief of Staff, BizOps lead, Strategy & Operations lead, or equivalent to a founder/CEO or a senior exec
  • Top pedigree. Strong academic background and time at companies with a known high bar, plus a record of being promoted inside them. We look hard at both
  • Left brain. You're fluent in a spreadsheet and comfortable in a data environment. You can build a model, size an opportunity, read a cohort curve, and pull your own numbers rather than filing a ticket and waiting
  • Right brain. You write exceptionally well. Memos, board decks, exec comms. You can take a messy 90-minute discussion and turn it into one page that changes what people do
  • You've run an operating cadence (OKRs or equivalent, weekly business reviews, planning cycles) at a company doing real volume, not as a theory from a deck
  • Backbone. You will regularly tell senior, accomplished people that their goal isn't measurable or their project is late. You do it without drama and without flinching, and they respect you for it
  • Startup metabolism. High ambiguity, fast context switching, nothing beneath you. You'd rather own the outcome than protect the org chart
  • You use AI tooling daily to move faster on analysis, drafting, and research

Bonus

  • DTC, subscription, or CPG experience, especially a business with recurring revenue and real retention mechanics
  • Consulting, banking, or PE foundation plus real operating experience (we're not looking for one without the other)
  • You've built materials for and presented to a board or investors
  • SQL, or enough of it to be dangerous

What this role is not

  • Not an executive assistant. You are not managing a calendar or booking travel
  • Not a project manager who takes notes and updates a tracker
  • Not a strategy role that stops at the recommendation
  • Not a functional leadership role. You won't inherit a team on day one, though this role can grow into one

If you want a clear lane and a stable scope, this isn't it, and that's fine.

How To Apply

Skip the cover letter. Instead, send us:

  • One page on an operating cadence you built or ran. What existed before, what you changed, and what measurably improved as a result
  • A time you told an executive something they didn't want to hear. What you said, and what happened
  • Short answer: A subscription business is seeing retention slip. Five executives each have a confident, different theory as to why. You have two weeks. What do you look at first, how do you get to the actual answer, and how do you land it with a leadership team that's already made up its mind?

We read these carefully. Applications without them won't move forward.

Benefits

  • Strong base, performance bonus
  • Meaningful equity because we want you to own a piece of what you build
  • Health benefits + health stipend
  • Generous time off
  • Free product

Product Manager

About Oula

Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems â including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health â to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

The Role

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR â it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.

We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack â including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.

You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver. You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.

What You'll Own

EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems

  • Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
  • Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
  • Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert â FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
  • Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
  • Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
  • Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch

Product Operations & Launch

  • Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations â standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
  • Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
  • Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
  • Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows

Standards & Knowledge Management

  • Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable â documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
  • Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
  • Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets

Data & Reporting

  • Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
  • Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
  • Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

What You Bring

  • 3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work â ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
  • Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity â you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
  • Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines â ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
  • Ability to speak âmultiple languagesâ â comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
  • Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.

At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.

At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.

Oula is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone's contributions are valued.
